docs.title: Remopy for FontLab
docs.text:
Control FontLab from external Python through its authenticated native MCP bridge, or from Glyphs through a standard-library client. Remopy supplies reusable synchronous and asynchronous sessions, JSON function transport, launch and script submission. It does not depend on AI libraries or agent prompts.

Start with installation, then the complete API, CLI and Glyphs reference. Read development and safety before calling a mutating tool. See the proprietary licence.

A client timeout leaves the execution outcome unknown. It does not cancel FontLab code, and timed-out mutations must never be retried automatically. Ordinary source tests, installed artifacts and native host acceptance are separate results.

The website is built from maintained Markdown without importing the product, starting clients or servers, or contacting FontLab. Its configured site URL is a future repository identity; private Pages publication remains owner-held.

docs.title: API, sessions and command line
docs.text:
Name What it does FontLab(command=None, timeout=30) Synchronous client; use as with FontLab() as fl:. command is the bridge executable, timeout seconds per call AsyncFontLab(command=None, timeout=30) Same operations as async with and await fl.run(code, **vars) Run Python in FontLab; returns ExecutionResult(value, stdout, stderr); set result to return a value fl.eval(expression, **vars) Evaluate one expression; returns the JSON value fl.execute_script(path, **vars) Run a .flpy/.vfpy file, __file__ set to its resolved path fl.tool(name, **arguments) / fl.tools() Call any native tool by name / list the live catalogue with schemas. Unknown argument names raise ValueError (FontLab would drop them silently); the master argument is master_name fl.fonts(), fl.output(), named controls Open fonts; recent captured output; the catalogue tools listed below @fl.python Run a decorated function remotely with JSON arguments and result enable_mcp() Inside FontLab: set mcp.enabled and notify the host (no save()) ensure_ready(app=..., command=None, timeout=30) Synchronous native launch and bounded MCP readiness; one setup macro when unavailable setup_mcp(), launch(), submit_script(), find_bridge() Launch FontLab, enable MCP from outside, locate the bridge call_tool(), run_python(), execute_script(), probe_tools() One-shot async functions for single calls

Errors: NativeExecutionError (a tool or the remote Python failed; .payload has type, message, traceback and partial output), ResultTransportError (the result could not be recovered; the call may have run), ValueError (bad timeout, variable name or oversized code), FileNotFoundError (no bridge executable), RuntimeError (used outside a context, or after a timeout until you open a fresh one), and TimeoutError (the call exceeded timeout; the outcome is unknown, so check FontLab before repeating).

Two different time limits apply. timeout is how long this client waits for one MCP call. FontLab's run_python tool also enforces its own fixed five-second execution deadline, which Remopy cannot change: code passed to run, eval or a @fl.python function must finish within it, so split longer work into short calls and read the resulting state. Remote code is limited to 32768 bytes and its output to 65536 bytes.

One context reuses one authenticated MCP connection. Idle time has no deadline; each initialization/call has the configured timeout (30 seconds by default). This synchronous API also works in notebooks with an existing event loop. It owns a dedicated AnyIO portal thread and releases its bridge on context exit or close(). AsyncFontLab exposes the same operations with async with and await; enter and exit that context on the same task. Calls are serialized. After timeout/cancellation, queued/new calls fail until a fresh context opens. The original one-shot async functions (call_tool, run_python, execute_script, probe_tools) retain their existing result shapes.

run returns ExecutionResult(value, stdout, stderr); set result in ordinary Python to return a value. eval returns the value directly. Context methods execute_script(path, **variables) preserve the resolved filename. JSON data is bound into an isolated namespace; fontlab, fontgate, fontpr, and PythonQt are prebound when available. Explicit variables take precedence. Imports/names from FontLab's global script scope are not inherited or changed. Python streams are captured during execution; concurrent Python threads share those interpreter streams. Native Output is never cleared. Unicode text, including U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029, round-trips unchanged in values, captured streams and native exception messages; only LF frames envelopes.

@fl.python preserves the local function signature and metadata, binds defaults locally, and transports arguments/results as JSON. Put imports inside the body. Globals/closures, async function bodies, unavailable source, native object results, and non-JSON values fail clearly; notebook source limitations can use run/eval. Native exceptions retain type/message/traceback and partial output in NativeExecutionError.payload. Truncated/missing/unsupported JSON results raise ResultTransportError. The wrapper counts toward native 32768-byte code and 65536-byte output bounds; FontLab's fixed five-second execution deadline is unchanged. A timeout leaves execution outcome unknown and never triggers retry.

Named controls include fonts, current_font, current_glyphs, glyph("A"), font_info, font_metrics, glyph_metrics, list_actions, run_actions, output, font open/new/save/close/activation and metric setters. Mutating calls perform the requested native operation. tool(name, **arguments) accesses the whole live catalogue; tools() gives its current schemas. output() reads MCP's recent capture; eval("fontlab.GetProperty('output')") reads the full native Output. The checkout provides examples/control.py for ordinary Python and examples/native_smoke.py for a read-only one-shot async check; their source is not rendered here. App's native UI example creates a native panel, modeless dialog and removable Preview drawing from @fl.python functions; --typerig composes a real TypeRig widget. Install Fontlabapp (and optionally typerig) in the host first. The example retains its native handles across calls, waits outside the UI thread, and removes only its own resources in finally.

execute_script() reads .flpy/.vfpy source, preserves its resolved filename as file, and verifies the native run_python success payload. Native errors raise NativeExecutionError with the original payload. call_tool() returns the actual SDK result, including real errors. FontLab's fixed execution deadline remains unchanged. Timeouts leave a mutation's outcome unknown; operations are never automatically retried.

launch() requests native macOS or Windows application launch. submit_script() requests a file open and returns execution_verified=False: submission alone cannot prove execution. Windows callers can select the full FontLab executable path with app; MCP uses the matching bridge executable.

ensure_ready(app=..., command=None, timeout=30) waits for the authenticated catalogue before returning. One finite startup deadline covers launch, setup and catalogue discovery. An unavailable host receives one nonce-confirmed setup macro; only read-only catalogue probes retry, and user operations are never replayed. An already reachable host needs no preference change. A modal startup dialog may prevent the first macro from executing and require manual dismissal; a missing or crashing bridge is not repaired by this helper.

setup_mcp() submits one unique .vfpy macro, verifies a nonce-matched native completion marker, then authenticates the bridge and discovers the tool catalogue. Setup enables the extended mcp.enabled preference using load() and a host notification, and persists generalHideWarningDialogs = True. Failed/timeout setup retains local macro/status files for inspection; completion is unknown, so inspect the host before repeating. enable_mcp() updates only mcp.enabled when called inside FontLab. It does not call save() or clear application logs.

Discovery checks an explicit argument or FONTLAB_MCP_COMMAND, then the native bridge on PATH or the FontLab 9 bundle. The legacy AIDUS_FONTLAB_MCP_COMMAND variable remains accepted for migration. Paths containing spaces are preserved. An explicit missing executable never falls back to a different FontLab build.

fontlab-remopy launch
fontlab-remopy --timeout 15 setup
fontlab-remopy tools
fontlab-remopy execute example.flpy
fontlab-remopy call list_fonts

docs.title: Remote-control FontLab from Glyphs
docs.text:
glyphs/fontlab_remote.py runs inside Glyphs 3 or 4 (or any Python 3.8+) with the standard library only, so Glyphs' Python needs nothing installed. It starts FontLab's bundled fontlab-mcp bridge (which holds the authentication for FontLab's local server) and speaks MCP over its standard input/output, with a deadline on every read.

Install: copy the file into Glyphs' Scripts folder (Script > Open Scripts Folder, i.e. ~/Library/Application Support/Glyphs 3/Scripts/), then Script > Reload Scripts. FontLab must be running with external MCP clients enabled (Preferences > Aidus). Run Script > FontLab Remote Control to print FontLab's version and open fonts next to Glyphs' current font in the Macro panel. From your own Glyphs scripts:

from fontlab_remote import FontLabClient

with FontLabClient() as fl:
    print([t["name"] for t in fl.tools()])
    print(fl.call("list_fonts"))                  # any FontLab MCP tool
    print(fl.eval("2 + 40"))                      # a JSON value from FontLab Python
    fl.run_python("print(fontlab.CurrentFont())")  # output text

Tool errors, bridge exits (with the bridge's message) and missed deadlines raise FontLabError. FONTLAB_MCP_COMMAND selects another bridge. Glyphs' Python must be configured (Glyphs > Settings > Addons); a framework that no longer exists makes every Glyphs script fail before this one starts.

docs.title: MCP SDK compatibility
docs.text:
Remopy runs on both MCP SDK lines (mcp>=1.26,<3). mcp/compat.py holds the only differences it meets: v2's snake_case fields (is_error, next_cursor), wire dumps with by_alias=True, and v1's RootModel wrapper around JSON-RPC messages. Test both:

uv sync --extra test
./test.sh                                                        # locked SDK (2.x)
uv run --extra test --with "mcp==1.30.0" python -m pytest -q     # v1 line
uv run --extra test --with "mcp==1.26.0" python -m pytest -q     # v1 floor
uv build

The test suite (run against mcp 2.3.0, 1.30.0 and 1.26.0 at commit 907d014) covers reusable sync/async sessions, decorated functions, JSON/Unicode/stream transport, source failures, native error parsing, extended preference setup, normalization, real SDK framing and timeout child-process cleanup by PID. Envelope regressions cover Unicode separators, missing/duplicate/malformed and oversized results, and verify that decoding failures never replay operations. Historical installed/native receipts remain separate from the current source and website. Requalify setup, catalogue, nonce-verified script execution and launch on the actual supported host before claiming current native acceptance.

docs.title: Execution limits and ownership
docs.text:
The native run_python deadline is fixed at five seconds, with 32768-byte code and 65536-byte output bounds. A client wait timeout does not stop native execution; deferred event-loop work outlives the scheduling call. Never replay a mutation after timeout, cancellation or a result decoding failure. Inspect native state before choosing another operation; reopen a fenced session before new calls.

Do not clear native Output, global update queues or owner resources. fl.output() reads MCP's recent captured log; App's native output helper reads a different panel. Use owned fixtures and a document-free dedicated session for native mutation. Native UI examples now belong to App, including examples/native_ui.py; do not recreate a duplicate in Remopy. They require App installed in the host, retain their native handles across calls, wait outside the UI thread and release only their owned resources. Optional TypeRig composition remains a separate installed dependency and native qualification.

Native PythonQt instances reject new attributes; use QByteArray.data() instead of bytes(QByteArray). Disconnect owned signals before deleteLater(), and do not disconnect a receiver that holds both native-slot and bound-method handlers. Never close a font while its Save Changes dialog is open. A runaway host call or timeout is not proof that host work stopped. Use the workspace's guarded native runner for authorized native work; the website never invokes it.

docs.title: Public imports and compatibility paths
docs.text: Public FontLab and AsyncFontLab imports remain lazy. Remopy 2.0 removed the eight pre-1.2 module paths (control, controls, execution, functions, launch_api, mcp_api, mcp_compat, native); the CHANGELOG lists the replacement for each. The deprecated python -m fontlab_remopy.mcp_bridge <command> entry point and its normalize_result and relay imports remain compatible with saved MCP configurations; they emit a DeprecationWarning on stderr and never write to stdout, which carries MCP. The current relay entry point is python -m fontlab_remopy.mcp.relay <command>. SDK framing, authentication and spawning remain SDK-owned. Normalization preserves true tool errors and RPC errors; child cleanup timing does not change the native Python deadline.

docs.title: Website checks
docs.text:
Use a separate Python 3.13 environment and uv 0.13.7, install src_docs/requirements.txt with --require-hashes, then run sh src_docs/build.sh and python -m unittest discover -s tests_docs -v. The build uses the source commit's timestamp once for deterministic output. Every main push builds the exact source SHA, publishes a normal docs-only child only when output changes, then verifies the immutable source/output lineage and independently rebuilds all output. Private Pages permissions and requests remain disabled.

Source, ordinary installed origins, all three SDK suites, native behavior, canonical adoption and publication are distinct gates. Issue 123 remains paused. The website does not establish a fresh SDK or native result.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Use Python 3.11 or newer for Remopy. FontLab's host environment is arm64 Python 3.11; an x86_64 interpreter cannot be loaded into that host. External clients and the website build use separate environments.

From an authorized source checkout, install into an external Python environment:

uv venv --python 3.11
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python .

The runtime dependencies remain mcp>=1.26,<3 and anyio. Native application launch and file submission support macOS and Windows. On Windows the default application is %ProgramFiles%\Fontlab\FontLab 9\FontLab 9.exe; Python callers may pass a full executable path as app. Discovery checks an explicit bridge argument or FONTLAB_MCP_COMMAND, then PATH or the installed FontLab 9 application. The legacy AIDUS_FONTLAB_MCP_COMMAND remains accepted. A missing explicit executable never silently chooses a different FontLab build.

For Glyphs 3/4, use the separate standard-library script: its Python needs no Remopy installation. Python 3.8+ is the stated minimum; retained runs used Python 3.9 and 3.13. Configure Glyphs' Python framework before using its Scripts menu.

Inside FontLab, enabling MCP updates only the extended preference and notifies the host; it does not save all preferences or clear logs. Owner-managed installation, native preference changes and running a script require their own acceptance. This documentation build performs none of them.

docs.title: Current English browser payload
docs.text:
The browser-component record binds the retained MaterialX 10.1.8 browser assets to exact upstream notices, package archives and source maps. The first-party Apache terms do not replace these third-party terms.

The English-only omission manifest binds all 35 unused lunr-languages 1.20.0 helpers, including Wordcut and TinySegmenter. The build rejects theme/search-language, corpus, vendor-set/hash and local HTML-reference drift before removing them. Nine core vendor assets remain byte-identical. Historical complete outputs remain recovery evidence; omitted helpers are not represented as currently distributed or relicensed.

The main source map retains 211 preferred sources, including 128 exact NPM source matches; the worker map retains 13 sources, including Lunr 2.3.9. The exact clipboard distribution embeds its dependencies; select, good-listener and delegate retain their upstream README MIT link and Zeno Rocha attribution, without invented standalone licence text or dates. CSS maps retain source names without embedded source bodies.

Material Design icons retain the Pictogrammers notice and Apache 2.0 icon terms or specifically stated underlying terms; code is MIT. Font Awesome Free retains Fonticons attribution and CC-BY 4.0 terms. Octicons retains GitHub's MIT notice; Lucide retains ISC and inherited notices. Of 45 observed ordered SVG path tuples, 43 match installed MaterialX icon path tuples exactly, including fontawesome/solid/caret-down.svg used by --md-version-icon. Its unchanged CSS header identifies Font Awesome Free 7.1.0, Copyright 2025 Fonticons, Inc., and CC-BY-4.0 icon terms; the full Font Awesome notice remains available below. The official Font Awesome 7.1.0 NPM caret SVG has different raw path bytes from the installed icon and CSS. The two unmatched Lucide focus/download tuples retain their pinned SCSS attribution. No unchanged-primary SVG, whole-geometry or optimizer-recipe equivalence is claimed.

FontLab's shared theme and external font responses remain external HTTPS services. Their implementation/font bytes are not copied into this payload; reference notices below do not freeze future responses. Build dependencies and local/hosted publication have separate qualification.
